title: Frontend: JSON.stringify
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind JSON.stringify. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(value) without JSON.stringify. Serialize finite JSON primitives, arrays and objects in Object.keys order. Escape quotes, backslashes and control characters. Inputs are valid acyclic JSON.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Handle primitives, arrays, and own enumerable object keys recursively.
alternativeApproaches: Add toJSON and replacer semantics only after documenting their ordering and error behavior.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Escaped string; unsupported value in object vs array; shared object.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
